canonicalExplanation.summary: When you click a button, the event travels in three phases: **capture** (down from window to the target), **target**, then **bubble** (back up through every ancestor). Listeners run by default in the bubble phase, so a listener on a parent `<ul>` hears clicks from every child. That's **event delegation**: one listener, then `event.target.closest("button")` to find which button was clicked, and it works for buttons added later. `stopPropagation()` stops the journey; `preventDefault()` only cancels the browser's **default action** (following a link, submitting a form) and does not stop propagation.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A to-do list attaches a click listener to each delete button when the page loads. Buttons for new to-dos don't work, and re-rendering adds duplicate listeners that delete two items per click. One list listener uses event delegation and closest to handle buttons added later. In this lesson you'll trace propagation and implement a delegated interaction without duplicate handlers.

Does a click listener on the parent `<ul>` still run?", "options": ["No, preventDefault stops it", "Yes: preventDefault only cancels navigation; the event still bubbles"], "answer": 1, "why": "Default action and propagation are separate. Only stopPropagation stops the bubble."}

examples.title: One listener for every delete button
examples.situation: One list listener uses event delegation and closest to handle delete buttons added later.
walkthrough: **Problem:** per-button listeners miss new buttons and duplicate on re-render.
**One list listener:** the ul hears every click as it bubbles up and uses `closest("button[data-action='delete']")`.
**Check:** after adding a new item, clicking its Delete will remove exactly one li, and the listener count stays 1.
examples.result: Every delete button works, including ones added later, and each click removes one item.

examples.title: The link that still triggered the row
examples.situation: A table row opens a details panel on click. A "Download" link inside the row calls preventDefault to start a custom download, but the details panel opens too.
walkthrough: The click still bubbled to the row's listener.
Fix: call `event.stopPropagation()` in the link handler, or have the row ignore clicks where `event.target.closest("a")` is set.
examples.result: Clicking Download starts the download without opening the details panel.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: preventDefault also stops the event from reaching ancestor listeners.
misconceptions.correction: preventDefault only cancels the browser's default action. The event keeps bubbling to ancestors unless stopPropagation is called.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The link that still triggered the row", why did the row still react?

analogy.example: An event is like **a shout in a building**: it's heard in the room where it happened, then on each floor above as it travels up the stairwell (bubbling). Delegation is putting **one receptionist on the ground floor** who hears everything and asks "which room did that come from?" (closest).
limitations: Shouts fade; events reach every ancestor unless stopped.
preventDefault is like cancelling the fire drill, not muting the shout.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing a delegated click. Step 1, Target: event.target is button; phase is target. The click starts at the delete button that was pressed. remediation.explanation: Draw the element's ancestors as a ladder. The event climbs it after the target. Ask: **who listens on which rung, and did anyone call stopPropagation?** preventDefault doesn't remove rungs.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The link that still triggered the row".

recap.summary: To trace propagation and implement a delegated interaction, remember events go capture, target, then bubble up through ancestors. Put one listener on a stable parent and use event.target.closest to find the control, which also handles items added later. preventDefault cancels default actions only; stopPropagation stops the bubble.
